channel.description: Recent content in Rust on 梦兽编程

item.title: Why Rust Makes C++ Programmers Lose Sleep at Night: Lessons from My Migration Journey
item.description: A C++ developer with 5 years of experience shares real insights from switching to Rust. From memory safety to concurrency, these 10 features completely changed my perspective on systems programming

item.title: One if Made This Rust Filter 4x Slower: The CPU Was Guessing for You
item.description: Filtering 1M floats: why is keeping half the slowest case? I reproduced the HN-top branch-prediction experiment on Windows (i5-12400F, rustc 1.97.1): a branchless rewrite cut the worst case from 5.1ms to 1.5ms (3.4x faster) — and learned when the trick backfires

item.title: A 1000x Gap: How Google Used Rust to Push Memory-Safety Bugs Below 20% — and the Playbook You Can Copy
item.description: In 2025 Google disclosed that memory-safety vulnerabilities on Android fell below 20% for the first time, and Rust code carries roughly 1000x fewer memory-safety bugs per million lines than C/C++. This article breaks down why, shows a C/Rust use-after-free comparison, and gives an actionable checklist.

item.title: Ditch Arduino: Write Microcontrollers in Rust + Embassy — Blink an LED and Learn Async Bare-Metal Programming
item.description: Arduino uses C++, where a few dozen KB of RAM means array overruns and dangling pointers slip past the compiler. This guide gets you running Rust bare-metal (no_std) plus the Embassy async framework on a Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040): toolchain, Cargo.toml, memory.x, an async blink, and 5 beginner pitfalls.

item.title: Stop Hand-Rolling JWT Validation: Add Production-Grade Auth to Your Rust API with OIDC + Axum
item.description: Rolling your own JWT validation, 8 out of 10 people miss something: no alg=none guard, no aud/iss checks, hardcoded keys, no clock-skew tolerance. This guide builds an OIDC Bearer-token validation middleware in Axum — JWKS fetching, algorithm whitelist, iss/aud checks, clock-skew tolerance — plus the simplest way to plug into Keycloak or Auth0.

item.title: Debugging Rust in VS Code: A Complete launch.json Guide with Windows Measurements
item.description: Set up Rust debugging in VS Code: rustup's rust-lldb is not applicable to Windows MSVC; configure CodeLLDB and launch.json, then troubleshoot breakpoints.

item.title: Your 8,000-Line Rust Project Made rust-analyzer Index 2.5M Dependency Lines
item.description: Why rust-analyzer feels slow: a small Rust project can trigger gigabytes of dependency analysis. Includes three tuning levels and their trade-offs.

item.title: 11 Days, 64 AIs, 530K Lines of Code: A Complete Engineering Retrospective on Rewriting Bun from Zig to Rust
item.description: Jarred Sumner used Claude Fable 5 and 50 dynamic workflows to rewrite 535,496 lines of Zig into Rust in 11 days. An agent pipeline of 1 implementer + 2 adversarial reviewers, peaking at 1,300 lines of code per minute. This isn't 'AI helping you write code' — this is 'AI helping you make decisions.'

item.title: Building a B+Tree in Rust: What I Got Wrong Before Getting It Right
item.description: A walkthrough of design mistakes I made implementing a B+Tree in Rust — from treating all nodes as in-memory pointers to understanding database pages, buffer pools, and record IDs. For developers learning database internals or systems programming in Rust.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 3): Refactoring Tools into a Skill Registry with Traits
item.description: Part 3 replaces the Part 1 match dispatcher with a Rust trait system: Skill, Registry, DynSkill, schemars-generated JSON Schema, parallel calls, error classification, retries, hooks, and permission gates.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 4): State Machines for Multi-Step Tasks
item.description: Part 4 introduces state machines for multi-step tasks: Node trait, Graph runner, SQLite checkpointing, Interrupt suspend/resume, PermissionMode gates, and NodeHook cross-cutting logic.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 5): Multi-Agent Crews
item.description: Part 5 covers multi-agent collaboration: when to add agents and when not to. The Agent trait, Crew parallel/sequential dispatch, Router, debate protocol, and composing with Part 3's skill registry and Part 4's state machine.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust — Part 2: Structured Prompt Architecture and the Cache Boundary
item.description: Following Part 1's tool-calling loop, Part 2 dives into Agent system prompt architecture: Identity, Instructions, Output, Examples, and Context layers, plus Anthropic Prompt Caching and prompt fingerprinting for regression testing.

item.title: Rust + AWS Lambda: Secure Credential-Free Access with Workload Credentials
item.description: How Rust Lambdas automatically obtain temporary credentials via IAM roles — from IAM role creation, Rust code implementation to cargo-lambda deployment, a hands-on walkthrough of the AWS Workload Credentials Provider workflow.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust — The Tool-Calling Loop Explained
item.description: A deep dive into the core mechanism of AI agents: the tool-calling loop. Through a ~200-line Rust implementation, we break down how models gain the ability to act via tool use, and why the architecture behind Claude Code and GitHub Copilot is the same fundamental loop.

item.title: Rust-Written Lua Compiler Runs Scripts Natively on Bare-Metal Arduino
item.description: TinyLua: a zero-VM Lua native compiler written in Rust. Compiles Lua source directly to AVR/ARM machine code for Arduino bare-metal — no interpreter, no GC, no runtime. Scripting language performance at C level.

item.title: Why Does Async Rust Feel So Hard? A Deep Dive for Developers
item.description: Async Rust is powerful but frustrating. From ecosystem fragmentation and Pin/Unpin to cancellation safety and performance traps, this article breaks down the real pain points with visual diagrams and practical analogies.

item.title: Rust Smart Pointers Complete Guide: Box, Rc, and RefCell Explained with Code Examples
item.description: Master Rust smart pointers: Box, Rc, RefCell, and the powerful Rc<RefCell<T>> combo. Learn heap allocation, reference counting, and interior mutability through vivid analogies. Beginner to intermediate level.

item.title: tokio::select! Finally Gets rustfmt Support: A Hands-On Look at better_tokio_select
item.description: The tokio::select! macro has always been a blind spot for rustfmt. better_tokio_select uses match syntax to fix this, so your async Rust code can finally be auto-formatted.

item.title: Rust is Taking Over GPU Programming: 239K Lines Replacing the Entire CUDA Ecosystem
item.description: Oxide Computer released OxiCUDA, a pure Rust implementation of the complete NVIDIA CUDA software stack. 239K lines of safe Rust code, 28 crates, zero C toolchain. This is production-ready code, not a proof of concept.

item.title: Rust's #[must_use]: Making Sure Your Return Values Can't Be Ignored
item.description: Rust #[must_use] attribute explained: put it on structs, functions, or traits to force callers to handle critical return values. Compile-time warnings prevent transactions and payments from being silently dropped.

item.title: Rust 10x Faster Than Spring? I Ran the Benchmarks. The Truth Is More Complicated.

item.title: From Zero to 1.8M Connections: A Rust/Tokio Gateway's Real Scaling Journey

item.title: We Compared 6 Outage Reports Before We Understood What Async Rust Actually Prevents

item.title: Don't Underestimate Rust Enums: A Complete Hands-On Guide

item.title: Stop Rewriting! The Rust FFI Sandwich: Keep Your C Code Running While You Add Safety

item.title: 500 Lines of Rust, 10 Seconds to Train: How Simple Is Building a Neural Network from Scratch?

item.title: 4000 Pages Per Second: The Rust PDF Library That's Changing the Game
